lines.text: I'm here to meet new students at the platform. I'm not a specific college officer, and this is not an official welcome. What should I call you?
I'm a student orientation leader, not a specific person. Start with your hall, then eat, then the library. Your seminar room is past Bicentennial.
Feb start uses Feb Orientation. The Wednesday-through-Sunday span was on the orientation FAQ when this line was written, and the game will not pretend the dates never change.
The college's orientation page says first-generation students get focused programming. Ask for that track. I won't invent the schedule.
The college's orientation page says international students get focused programming. Ask for that track. I won't invent the schedule.
Most first-years, as of the admitted-student page fetched 2026-10-27, live in Stewart, Hepburn, Allen, Coffrin, or New Battell. Your real assignment comes from Residential Life, not from this game.
Unlimited meals means Proctor, Atwater, and Ross. The Grille, Crossroads, So-full Sips, the S.E.A. Dinette, and Midd Express were the retail names on the admitted-student page.

Crossroads is the student-run café in this library, per the admitted-student page fetched 2026-10-27. I can point you at Bicentennial when you are ready for a sample seminar. I am not a real librarian's portrait.
This is a sample seminar, not an official Middlebury section and not a real professor. Sit down and the lesson panel will teach one skill: how to ask a question.

Your support team, as the admitted-student page described it, includes your first-year seminar professor and pre-major advisor, a Compass Mentor, an orientation leader, and a residence director or assistant.
If the outdoors are your interest, I can clear you toward the trail stand-in. It is not a named mountain yet.
If languages are your interest, I can clear you toward the downtown stand-in. No shops are named until we have a source.
Downtown is still a placeholder. I will not invent businesses, hours, or which street to trust.
